analysis: The only change in docs/developer/test.md is at lines 1049-1050 (head): the SDK 27 release qualification text now says SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 (Xcode 27.2) and links to the `release` toolchain section of build.md, replacing the earlier SDK 27 / Swift 6.4 wording. This is a documentation-only change. It has no runtime, code, key, attestation, or authorization effect, and it does not touch the wire protocol, cache storage, or trust boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013) or the threats T-041 and T-053 through T-061. The surrounding unchanged text covers the add-on hold, App Attest dispatch, native serving qualification, and cluster tests. I did not re-review that text as a new change, and I found nothing in it that this edit contradicts. The edit does not claim any new physical qualification, and the surrounding text keeps the existing disclaimers: no real Apple service validation, and optional physical smoke. Unverified items: whether the build.md anchor `#sdk-27-release-builds-and-caches` exists, and whether the CI toolchain actually matches Xcode 27.2. These are external to the supplied evidence and are doc-accuracy questions, not security regressions. No threat-model update is needed from this change.
